issues.description: Interface name and type for the milking capability is inconsistent across artifacts. The problem statement and UML refer to a Milkable interface with method messageOnMilk(), and the template Main.java also references Milkable. However, the solution repository introduces a different interface named Dairy (with messageOnMilk()) and leaves a Milkable.java file empty. Additionally, animal classes in the solution implement Dairy rather than Milkable. This mismatch between Milkable and Dairy is a structural type/name inconsistency that will confuse students about which interface to implement and may break automated tests expecting Milkable.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the milking interface name and usage across all artifacts. Either: (a) rename the solution's Dairy interface to Milkable (move its messageOnMilk() signature into Milkable.java), and update animal classes to implement Milkable; or (b) update the problem statement and template to use Dairy consistently. Also ensure Milkable.java in the solution is not empty (remove it or implement it) so there is a single, correctly named interface for students to implement.

issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to an interface named 'Milkable' (expected to declare messageOnMilk()), but the solution implementation introduces an interface named 'Dairy' and has classes (Seal, Goat) implement Dairy. This inconsistent interface name (Milkable vs. Dairy) breaks the direct mapping from the exercise description/template to the solution and will confuse students about which interface to create/implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the interface name across all artifacts. Rename the solution's 'Dairy' interface to 'Milkable' (file Dairy.java -> Milkable.java), ensure it declares String messageOnMilk(), and update Seal and Goat to 'implements Milkable'. Remove or replace the empty Milkable.java in the solution repository so there is a single consistent interface named 'Milkable' matching the problem statement and template.
